schemaObservation.kind: supplemental MCP tools/list; not original native launch catalog

selected.name: work_items:get
selected.description: Read work-items by ID (`id` for one; `ids` for a batch). Returns `{ ok, results:[…], counts }`; correlate rows by id, not position. Batch reads also include a per-requested-ID receipt. Read `returns` for conditional warnings.

id.description: a single work-item id (n=1 shorthand for ids:[id])

attachments.description: Standalone one-item consented attachment read: {} lists metadata; id returns a base64 byte page (default 1024 bytes, max 2048). Canonical fixes resolve original report evidence. Expired evidence is unavailable.

ids.description: work-item ids for ordinary reads (1–100). With resume:true, provide one ID only; prefer the id argument for a continuation read.

harness.description: caller harness scope; do not copy a cross-hive row's canonical harness here

detail.description: also return topics, thread posts (comments), outgoing links, `lifecycle` — the unified history (blocks, holds, reopens) with a coverage report saying what is NOT recorded — and `priorAttempts`, the bounded prior-attempt brief (what was already tried on this item's plan lane, and what the budget OMITTED). Accepts `true`/`false`, or the aliases `'full'`/`'summary'` (some tools in this catalog use that string-enum convention instead).

checksOnly.description: return only the stored checkpoint check-row ledger (`checkpointChecks.rows` with caller-facing id/claim identities) plus recency/failure metadata; omit the checkpoint narrative and other enrichments. Use this before building `retireIds` instead of fetching the full checkpoint body.

checkpointOnly.description: standalone exact checkpoint text page for exactly one item; skips item payload and other enrichments. Pair with root-level offset (Unicode code points, default 0) and limit (default 512, hard cap 768); follow checkpointPage.nextOffset and compare checkpointContentHash across pages. checkpointPage:null means no stored checkpoint unless checkpointReadFailed is true.

offset.description: checkpointOnly page start measured in Unicode code points; omitted means 0. The returned checkpointPage.offset is clamped to totalChars.

limit.description: checkpointOnly page size in Unicode code points; omitted means 512. Larger requests are clamped to 768 and disclosed in checkpointPage.limitClamped.

resume.description: Standalone one-item continuation view: current claim, complete structured next action, saved checks and exact evidence references, with freshness and scoped recovery. Pass exactly one item (prefer id; a one-element ids array is accepted, but multi-id batches are rejected). Uses checkpoint:{did,left,next} written by work_items:checkpoint; missing/unreadable state remains explicit. Checks are at results[].resume.checks.rows (an array), not resume.checks; resume.checks.omitted counts saved rows excluded by the packet budget. Do not combine with detail, checksOnly, checkpointOnly, offset, limit, threadLimit, priorAttemptRefs, or operationalBrief; use a separate read for those enrichments.

operationalBrief.description: Add `operationalBrief` per row: claim/state, blockers, last verified evidence, next action and successor residue, projected from this same read. Unmeasured fields are explicit `unknown` with a reason, never zero. Forces a complete read; not with resume or checksOnly.

priorAttemptRefs.description: raw drill-down for the requested work-item(s): pass `id` (one) or `ids` (many) together with these refs. Resolve refs back to their FULL untruncated source records. When combined with `detail:true`, this replaces the bounded `priorAttempts` brief so the response does not mix clipped history with the raw records; make a separate read if you need both views. Take refs from a brief's `omission.omittedRefs` (records the budget could only COUNT) or from a clipped record's own `rawRef` — the brief names them precisely so a bounded read is never a dead end. Refs that no longer resolve come back in `unresolved[]`, which is an answer about the history, not an error.

threadLimit.description: return a bounded oldest-first recent-comment window instead of loading the full thread; 0 explicitly suppresses thread work, positive values return up to 10 posts with a same-snapshot total. The effective window is capped at 10: a larger value is CLAMPED (not rejected) and the result reports `threadLimitClamped:{requested,applied}` — read `threadWindow.total`, not `shown`, for how many posts exist.

inputSchema.x-papercusp-call-constraint: resume requires one item (pass `id`, or a one-element `ids` array; multi-id batches are not supported) and cannot be combined with detail, checksOnly, checkpointOnly, offset, limit, threadLimit, priorAttemptRefs or operationalBrief; use a separate read for those enrichments (two calls: work_items:get { id, resume:true } for the continuation, then work_items:get { id, detail:true } for the detail record)

schemaHashEncoding: UTF-8 JSON without whitespace in returned property order

currentBuildTestRoute.source: Committed local integration branch (staging by default), loaded by maintained staging sync
currentBuildTestRoute.isolation: Separate port, process and checkout; database and workspace are not isolated.
currentBuildTestRoute.verification: Measured :3170 build identity plus request/response on that build.

_projection.next: The emitted result was written to the reference in `content` — page it to inspect what the tool emitted. The `uri` in `content` is a framed scratch-reference container, not a raw JSON file. Read it with `capability:read` byte pages (`byte_offset` + `byte_limit`, without `raw`) and follow `next_cursor` to validate and unwrap its manifest before parsing the payload; the default numbered line view can truncate a long single-line payload. However, the emitted result already carries upstream partial marker(s) (textTruncated); paging this reference cannot recover the omitted fields, rows, or text. The dev:pipeline_position result already marked a field as truncated. Re-read using that field's documented recovery handle or narrower arguments; a wider per-field limit may not exist.
